problem:
Let $y={\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}$ be a series solution to the equation $6{y}^{′}+3xy=0.$

What is the recurrence relation for the coefficients ${a}_{n},$ where $n=1,2,3,…$
worked_solution:
First, we find ${y}^{′}(x):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(x) & ={({\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n})}^{′} \\  & ={({a}_{0}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n})}^{′} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now we substitute the expressions for $y(x)$ and ${y}^{′}(x)$ into the given differential equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}6{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1}+3x{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n} & =0 \\ {\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }6n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1}+{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }3{a}_{n}{x}^{n+1} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

We want to make the powers of $x$ the same. Therefore, in the first sum, we change the index of the summation by writing $m=n-1.$ This gives

$$
{\sum }_{m=0}^{\infty }6(m+1){a}_{m+1}{x}^{m}+{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }3{a}_{n}{x}^{n+1}=0.
$$

Now, in the second series, we change the index of the summation by writing $m=n+1.$ This gives

$$
{\sum }_{m=0}^{\infty }6(m+1){a}_{m+1}{x}^{m}+{\sum }_{m=1}^{\infty }3{a}_{m-1}{x}^{m}=0.
$$

Replacing $m$ with $n$ in both summations (since it does not matter which letter we use) gives

$$
{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }6(n+1){a}_{n+1}{x}^{n}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }3{a}_{n-1}{x}^{n}=0.
$$

Next, we need to get two series starting with the same value of $n.$ So, we take out the term $n=0$ from the left-hand side:

$$
6{a}_{1}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }6(n+1){a}_{n+1}{x}^{n}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }3{a}_{n-1}{x}^{n}=0
$$

We now combine the series, as follows:

$$
6{a}_{1}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }[6(n+1){a}_{n+1}+3{a}_{n-1}]{x}^{n}=0
$$

Finally, by equating coefficients of ${x}^{n},$ we obtain

$$
{a}_{1}=0,\,6(n+1){a}_{n+1}=-3{a}_{n-1}.
$$

Solving for ${a}_{n+1}$ gives

$$
{a}_{n+1}=-\frac{{a}_{n-1}}{2(n+1)},\,n=1,2,3,….
$$

Note that every coefficient with an odd index is equal to $0,$ since ${a}_{1}=0.$
